notes.title: Locations 🌍 Fable Hospital
notes.content:
Greetings, future managers of medieval fantasy hospitals!

After discussing the possible events that may occur while running your hospital, it's time to talk about one of the most important factors that will shape your management: location.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

The world is vast, and each place where you establish your hospital will have unique characteristics and challenges that you must face to keep everything running smoothly. Temperature, natural disasters, epidemics, and region-specific diseases will put your skills as an administrator to the test.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/1e2e1f7f620233dad6917f612547ae096efe0e4d.png

Here are the various corners of the world where you will have to set up your medieval hospital.

France
In the heart of the Old World lies a land synonymous with the medieval era. A place filled with knights, bards, charming princes, sleeping princesses, kings, and queens. But even royalty falls ill, and your hospital will see patients ranging from the noblest aristocrats to the humblest peasant.

North America
North America: A land where breathtaking landscapes meet harsh terrain, and mysticism collides with the rising industrial reality. Scorching days and freezing nights will put your management skills to the test. Run your hospital wisely… or you might end up seeing your face on a "Wanted" poster.

Egypt
The heart of the Nile and the land of the gods. The desert shows no mercy to anyone, and it won’t be any different for your hospital, so it wouldn’t hurt to add a few fans. Mummies will visit your hospital, and not because of a lack of bandages.

Norway
This cold land is home to very tough people… but they get sick too. No one is immune to a cold, not even the Vikings. It wouldn’t hurt to add a few bonfires to prevent your patients from turning into ice cubes.

Spain
Managing a medieval fantasy hospital on the Iberian Peninsula can be fun, but it’s also challenging. Many patients will arrive at your clinic, including some who claim to be knights from a place whose name I’d rather not remember.

Mexico
Running a medieval fantasy hospital is quite the challenge, where the jungle and mysticism come together. Pirates and skeletons roam the region, and your patients might come with all sorts of issues

Japan
In the Land of the Rising Sun, where both earthly beings and spirits coexist, you'll need to be prepared to face the unexpected. Your skills will be constantly put to the test. Honor is everything here—if you fail, your reputation may never recover.

Transylvania
A land of legends, where the sun doesn’t shine often and is ruled by a strange count. You’ll encounter patients of all kinds, most of them cursed. The good news is they’re easy to diagnose... the bad news, you’ll see for yourself.

Greece
You’ll have to attend to many "mythological patients," some more friendly than others. Most of them are this way due to a curse or the will of the Olympian Gods, so they’re not in the best of moods... treat them with care.

Denmark
With its relentless cold and gray skies, is a place where ghost legends persist. Ancient castles and deserted streets seem to hide spirits, creating a mysterious and eerie atmosphere.

Mongol Empire
In this land of endless plains, the wind roams free… and so do the orcs. With nomadic warriors and formidable beasts wandering the steppe, your hospital must always be ready.

Albion
Old Albion is the land of fairy tales par excellence. You’ll have to treat legendary beings, from dark fairies to unicorns with strange ailments, whose cures will require a blend of magic and science.

Atlantis
The most magical and legendary place where you'll have to manage your fantasy hospital. In the middle of the ocean rises a majestic city, home to forgotten wonders and climates as diverse as its mysterious inhabitants.

No matter where you choose to build your hospital in Fable Hospital, each location will bring its own challenges, mysteries, and unique patients. 

From lands of myths and legends to cities submerged in the ocean, managing it won’t be easy. But with ingenuity and courage, you can turn your hospital into a refuge for heroes, fantastical creatures, and unfortunate souls in need. Are you ready for the challenge?

notes.title: Events & Merchants 💰 Fable Hospital
notes.content:
Greetings, future manager of medieval fantasy hospitals!

In the last Steam event, we talked about the importance of upgrades and research you can do with the help of your alchemist in your hospital. Now, we’ll dive into something a bit more random...

In Fable Hospital, no map is the same as another. Each region has its own unique biome, with its own resources, extreme climates, and unpredictable conditions.

Did you expect it to rain in the desert? Well, think again... Your water reserves won’t refill with rain because it simply doesn’t rain.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Want to plant crops in the snow? Good luck. Production will be minimal, if you get anything at all. That’s why the wandering merchant will be your best ally (or your worst headache).

The Wandering Merchant
The wandering merchant will appear randomly on any map —forget about memorizing dates— to buy and sell vital resources: food, water, healing plants...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/0e9e90474d4f180ec0717a68205e116317f15ba7.gif

Because no, not all your money will go into building hospitals: if you don’t have supplies, you can’t heal anyone!

But that’s not all, the very mother nature of each map will put you to the test with natural and weather events.

Natural and Weather Events
Each map brings unique natural events: earthquakes, floods, rainstorms...

Yes, they’ll destroy structures. But not all is bad: over time, a flooded area will become more fertile.

And beware of the weather: sandstorms, polar cold, heatwaves, snowstorms...

Make sure you have water and wood reserves if you don’t want your hospital to turn into a freezer or an oven.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/5e6e4e6470e6a05e3f068df8b4b50133d26d41c7.gif

Remember, in Fable Hospital, you don’t just manage a hospital, you survive and adapt to an unpredictable world. Stay alert and make sure you’re prepared for the unexpected!

notes.title: Talents & Upgrades 💡 Fable Hospital
notes.content:
Hello, future manager of medieval hospitals!

In the previous event, we talked about resource management—how to gather, store, and use resources wisely so your medieval hospital doesn't collapse in the middle of a plague.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Today, we're diving deeper into another key aspect of survival in Fable Hospital: Research and upgrades.

Research, upgrades, and critical decisions in Fable Hospital

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/a6d38259d5ed6337a494bcba2d8ae19390a35dc8.gif

In Fable Hospital, it’s not enough to receive patients—you have to figure out what’s wrong with them. The craziest and most surreal diseases can only be diagnosed if you let our mad alchemist run his experiments. Just be warned… the results can be unpredictable (and explosive).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/7363723bed1e0f1e289da7b4e82448ec64c6b227.gif

Train your staff
Improving your workers' skills makes them more efficient—and also cheaper. A well-trained team is a happy team… and a cost-effective one.

Strange machines, essential treatments
Treating diseases requires machines as peculiar as the illnesses themselves. Don’t forget to maintain and upgrade them, or things might get out of hand.

Optimize resource production
From potions to magical ingredients, everything can be produced more efficiently. Explore different ways to improve your production chains.

Spend wisely… or lose the game
Research and upgrades aren’t cheap. Choosing what to develop at each level can make the difference between success and total disaster. Consider the map, the biome, and your available resources before making your decisions.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/e53eb8c5ae24956774707c3aa22ed3ae50589d8e.gif

Knowledge is power—and in Fable Hospital, it’s also the key to survival.

notes.title: Resource Management 🌾 Fable Hospital
notes.content:
Hello, future manager of medieval hospitals!

In our last development diary, we talked about VIP characters and what it means when they visit our hospital. In this new entry, we’re diving into one of the most crucial aspects of running a hospital: resource management.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Running a medieval hospital isn’t easy! In Fable Hospital, every resource matters, and you’ll rely on your wit (and your goblins) to keep things running smoothly.

Essential Ingredients, Extraordinary Results

Gather water, chop wood, and grow essential ingredients to brew healing potions, craft artisanal beer, and even cook up some hearty cabbage soup. Our expert nuns can’t perform miracles without raw materials!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/0a288e3a3e73be5c2f71d00551920a26178ba33c.gif

Smart farming

Manage production queues, rotate your crops, and avoid shortages of key supplies. You never know when an emergency—or a flood—might strike.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/9b6e9948883699188653e1e717a8a4f5221f026d.gif

The weather changes everything

Hot weather? You’ll need extra water. Freezing cold? Burn more wood to keep the hospital warm. The environment directly affects your production, so plan ahead!

Our loyal goblins

They handle all the gathering and crafting. They don’t complain (too much) and will work tirelessly... as long as there’s some warm soup waiting for them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/7fe60580cb8923e5ce750a32142f0c8230eec19b.gif

Are you ready to become the kingdom’s greatest hospital manager?

notes.title: New VIP Characters 👑 Fable Hospital
notes.content:
Hello, future manager of medieval hospitals!

In previous development diaries, we have shared who your future employees and patients will be. In today’s update, we introduce you to a special type of character: the VIP visitors!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

From time to time, we will receive special visits for which we must be prepared. An ancient and powerful figure will come from their earthly or celestial realm to drop by our hospital and see how things are going. And it’s best to be prepared: they are profoundly demanding of their subjects (not so much of themselves).

We might receive visits from:

Zeus ⚡
This Greek god is as powerful as he is capricious. When he descends from Olympus, let’s hope he approves of what you’re doing with your hospital… or lightning might strike twice in the same place.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/ecd6ab9117f642cad51ca98a5d42a4292d788943.png

Odin ❄️
His ravens tell him everything, but sometimes the Allfather likes to step down from his throne in Asgard and visit your hospital personally.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/8307a4aa77324731ca44122834f538054c4f8453.png

Ra ☀️
The God of the Sun, after battling Apophis every night, comes to check how you're managing your hospital—just in case he needs healing. You’d better keep him satisfied; the desert heat will be the least of your worries.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/5713eb52489beb255f40007703e6ef46a02725ff.png

Hades 🔥
The God of the Underworld rarely leaves the Abyss. As the busiest Olympian, he wants to make sure your hospital runs smoothly—so he doesn’t get more clients in his realm.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/bb3b3acb6e07dc25ec2e4922729f2bcf8d4177d4.png

Quetzalcoatl 🦅
The Feathered Serpent descends to observe your hospital. Quetzalcoatl, bearer of knowledge and life, expects medicine to flourish in your realm… or perhaps the gods of the underworld will have more work than necessary.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/a2076b07ee58157e80b66338ab0f7a8abf634c0e.png

Inari 🦊
Inari’s spirits wander through your hospital. The god of prosperity watches to see if your management is worthy of his blessings… or if the sick will end up begging for a miracle.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/278637d363a6e3ed431095e33069603cdd5c5f28.png

King Arthur 🗡️
King Arthur has arrived from Camelot to see if your hospital is worthy of legend. He's a bit upset because he couldn't pull Excalibur from the stone, so he took the stone with him to remain King. Will you prove yourself a true ruler of medicine.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/e9ef3034dfd7be92cae61e1dbf07fe06a4561f0b.png

VIP characters add an extra layer of depth to managing your hospital. This gives you an additional incentive to always strive for optimal performance, presenting a constant challenge that rewards you generously when everything runs as it should (or almost does). However, be careful—if they are not pleased, they might not just withhold their rewards but also make your job even more difficult.

notes.title: New Doctors 💉 Fable Hospital
notes.content:
Hello medieval hospital manager,

The surreal roster of doctors present in Fable Hospital welcomes its newest addition, The Executioner!

Even executioners can reinvent themselves as doctors. This specialist doesn't hesitate, doesn't flinch, and above all, doesn't use anesthesia. His diagnosis is quick—and so is his treatment. They say he has a steady hand. A little too steady.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/fcb6b7cbeece1307fff77e4f7ef23798cdf5a54b.png

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Take a look to the rest of the roster of Doctors & Workers here:

DOCTORS
[expand type=details expanded=false]
Plague Doctor

The only person with knowledge slightly similar to medicine. He cures 50% of his patients and kills the other 50%, a surprisingly better average than his colleagues. He is also obsessed with cleanliness and hygiene. He is the only doctor who always washes his hands.

Druid

His favorite remedies are infusions and music. Unfortunately for his patients, his infusions taste like dirt, and his musical abilities are on par with those of a deaf cat. To a druid, magic and gardening are the same thing. He never feels bad when he loses a patient; they serve as fertilizer for his plants.

Alchemist

The world's foremost expert in succeeding by failing. The worse his formulas' results, the more likely they are to end up curing the patient. Side effects are... secondary. Who cares if your skin changes color, the number of fingers on one hand isn't usual, or you lose an ear? The important thing is getting cured. It may not cure you, but it might make you rich by turning you into gold.

Fortune Teller

She is a master of future knowledge. But she can't differentiate between the important parts and the trivial details. Well, no one is perfect. By the way, her obsession with the evil eye as the cause of all known diseases doesn't help.

Mad Engineer

He is convinced that he will change the world with his next invention. And he certainly will: to a smokier and more explosion-filled place. Skilled like few others in the art of creating things that almost work. He despises the weakness of flesh. You may enter the operating room for a wrist surgery and leave with a steam-powered mechanical arm.

Torturer

He doesn't like being called a torturer, he prefers chiropractor. When you hear him talk about "alternative therapies," you know what he means. He is the best at making his patients talk, though always in an incomprehensible manner. "If it hurts, it means it's healing" as a way of life

Friar

Always willing to pray for your soul and your health. A staunch defender of moderation with a glass of wine in hand. He has a tendency to prescribe "a fun afternoon" as a cure for almost everything (this afternoon includes large amounts of wine). With a maxed-out faith build, he fully believes that divine power can cure everything, even what medicine can't touch.

Nun

Ancient healing methods, recipes with centuries of "proven" effectiveness. They dedicate their lives to caring for others as long as your health improves quickly; their patience runs out quickly (especially if a friar drinks their wine). The plants they use for healing also serve them to make a delicious salad, whenever the occasion allows.

Wizard

He is wise and reflective, always invoking the right magic, though his healing spells leave a slight burning smell on the patients. Before joining the hospital, he was a professor at a famous magic school—until a small "explosive accident" in potions class cost him his job. He dresses like a solemn wizard, but his true specialty is card tricks.[/expand]

WORKERS
[expand type=details expanded=false]
Gatherer Goblins

They work tirelessly and never talk about working conditions. By working, they mean collecting all kinds of things. And by all kinds of things, I mean EVERYTHING, even those that have an owner. Their concept of ownership is, let’s say... flexible. 

Baker

She is capable of turning flour, water, and yeast into a healing miracle. Sometimes she even adds sugar, though no one is sure if it's too much. Most of her bread is so hard that you could knock down a troll with a single blow, but that's a minor detail. As they say, half a loaf is better than none.

Hunchback Janitor

Frighteningly efficient in keeping the hospital clean. His cleaning method inevitably involves scaring the patients, which doesn’t make him very popular among them. However, he has an inexplicable love for ringing the bells, which has become one of his daily routines. While he is the favorite of rats and other rodents, he has a strange animosity toward the friar, creating tension whenever they cross paths.

Recepciónists

These undead are in charge of organizing patients in the hospital. They are very professional, though a bit arrogant. They speak three languages: Sarcasm, limited patience, and "not my problem."

Brewmaster

The most beloved employee in the hospital, both by doctors and patients. He prescribes beer as a cure as easily as he samples his own brews. His only weak point is his inability to measure the potency of his beer, which usually has more degrees than a stew in August.

Leprechaun

His storytelling skills reach unimaginable limits: some patients manage to get cured just by listening to him narrate, while the rest simply fall asleep. The problem? His fondness for practical jokes. The poor patients who fall asleep often end up with their faces marked. Additionally, he likes gold and rainbows, which leads him to always seek out the brightest things in every corner of the hospital.[/expand]

notes.title: New Patients 🤒 Fable Hospital
notes.content:
Greetings future managers of medieval fantasy hospitals!

Fable Hospital is a management game where you take charge of a hospital in a medieval fantasy world. And aren’t patients what gives meaning to every good hospital?

Prepare yourself, because your hospital will be visited by the most outrageous, bizarre, and unique patients, suffering from equally strange diseases that only science, magic (or sometimes a mix of both) can cure. We present you with new patients that you will have to treat in Fable Hospital:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Quixote
He thinks he is a chivalrous knight in shining armor with a magical helmet, but the truth is that he just bought second hand stuff! He often visits the hospital due to his frequent battles with windmills, although he doesn't know why. The curious thing is, he always loses.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/6d45171069cd259b46cbe1ae9f40c880209415e2.png

Cyclops
Although he is very strong, he always has vision problems. He just wants to be left alone, but there's always a young hero-in-training who picks a fight with him. The good thing is that he spends half as much on an optometrist.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/9bf386eef357735429d051bd16d83ff4d0c71006.png

Unicorns
Pride and arrogance turned into a mythical creature. It is said that his magical horn can heal others of their ailments, but it seems he cannot heal his own... ironic.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/4ebea32af15551a3590a9e9ca0ced79bfbdbe227.png

These are just some of the many new patients waiting for you in Fable Hospital. You'll have to treat samurais, ghosts, elves, vikings, clerics, and many more.

Decapitated
The great advantage of this patient is that his "illness" is easy to diagnose. It’s obvious at first glance. The problem? Well, he doesn’t like being stared at, and his head is not attached to the rest of his body. He requires rather bold remedies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/9a9aed9487ae54e32255240aec5b4e722b7d7b16.png

Zombie
The kind of patient that doctors love the most: never complains, and if they do, it’s completely unintelligible. They don’t need anesthesia, or at least it seems so. Almost all advantages, the big challenge is enduring the smell they emit—or trying to avoid being bitten.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/ddb852e9af67e5ec652769ab1b102543b144992c.png

Skeleton
Everyone thinks that in his previous life he was a pirate, but no one has been able to confirm it. No one knows either if his previous life had anything to do with his current illness: the complete lack of skin, organs, and muscles. He never parts from his hat, which might be the only one piece left of him.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/a05a7b27e418eb7cfe7c9281dbcffc23c929a3cb.png

Dark Fairy
She’s going through a phase, or at least that’s what her parents claim. As for her, she vehemently denies it. Butterfly wings, a black heart. She flies but not much, never rises more than a few centimeters off the ground. "I’ve become so numb," she murmurs, as if her spirit is trapped in the air around her.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/16e6502a0da41ce1a6953f868687379910599135.png

Minotaur
They are usually unbearable: they think of themselves as living legends, narcissistic to the extreme. To their credit, they have millennia-old anecdotes. They have a strange obsession with red fabrics and labyrinths.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/d4a4be1e77b0ec60be7bebfdd68603b9c80fa669.png

Mummy
The quintessential elderly patient. He is (literally) older than the pyramids. His joints creak as if they haven’t moved in 4000 years. And most likely, that’s the case. He’s the only patient who already comes bandaged from home. He tries to play with the doctors a millennia-old card game that no one remembers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/327509b395707a6af2f6942f9683d8c6c19285ce.png

Orc
He has the intellectual capacity of a rock. Adding two plus two is a challenge for him. The mind of a 2-year-old in the body of an Olympic weightlifting champion. Weapons are not allowed in the hospital, but no one has dared to enforce this rule with him. He’s very territorial in the waiting room with other orcs.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/745f8f3eb06416140d839ddab4c3cfeaa3e40918.png

Possessed
Everyone knows there is something evil inside her body, but no one really knows what. Her gaze competes in coldness with her heart. Practically all doctors fear her (due to her bad temper). She never parts from her teddy bear (unfortunately, it smells awful). The teddy bear even tells her to do things, and she listens without question.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/f3a47000c51361093b10087d6495ba9825d5c3ff.png

Werewolf
He has a love-hate relationship with the moon. The most hated by the rest of the patients: he spends the night howling and doesn’t let anyone sleep. Feeding him is more expensive than any treatment he receives. And on more than one occasion, they confuse his doctor’s hand with a food dish. It’s not a good idea for him to cross paths with the vampires in the waiting room. Despite all that, he’s a good boy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/0ed73fc5312461c603b8b7b9e8c6393b94527c95.png

Vampire
The living (or almost) proof that vampires exist. He dresses and behaves like an aristocrat, but no one takes him seriously. He thinks he is much scarier than he actually is (not at all). He tries unsuccessfully to scare the hospital staff, usually making a fool of himself with his refined manners. He is very vain but can’t see himself in mirrors, and has a strange rivalry with the werewolves.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/85227fa8c40f0cc215c5164050e41642230c6f3a.png

notes.title: Locations 🌍 Fable Hospital Dev Diary #4
notes.content:
Hello future manager of medieval hospitals,

In today's development diary, we're sharing a fundamental aspect of Fable Hospital: the locations. As you might expect, the location of your hospital will be crucial in managing it.

But before we continue! Don't forget to add Fable Hospital to your wishlist, unless you want a nighttime visit from the Werewolf 🐺

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Each region will test your management skills, as each comes with its own challenges and sometimes even advantages. Resources and temperature vary drastically from one region to another. So, it’s essential that you know how to adapt to the conditions. And quickly, because a frozen patient is a lost patient (or is it?).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/56329ace67e7d7530f2fcbe4a4fb800567c2ae7b.png

Below, we share four of them, out of the 13 that will be in Fable Hospital.

Egypt

The cradle of an ancient civilization with a strange obsession for piling rocks in pyramid shapes. Its arid and dry climate poses a challenge for resource gathering. Luckily, the great Nile River is perfect for cooling off and is home to the friendliest crocodiles in the world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/b9037ba15840b609738737bef65bbb1670c9fbce.png

Scandinavia

Northern Europe is characterized by its cold climate. Very cold. Seriously, very, very, very cold. You'll have to figure out how to keep your hospital at a temperature reasonable for human life (and for other races, of course).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/03bf07a08108b381555913990f6b60312a6bd47a.png

North America

The mythical Wild West, with much more wild than west. Its nomadic natives also need hospital services. The land is desert-like, full of prickly cacti, and surrounded by mountains of a strange reddish color.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/cf1fc8f816604b81736245277d35b15a57e4b8d0.png

France

Here, the climate is mild and gentle, without major temperature challenges. The rivers and frequent rains make the land fertile, perfect for agriculture and abundant in resources. But not all the news is good: occasionally, you might run into a French person.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/4e37569189df64c40c0e5495f1e7a2ac6076de59.png

Interesting? Follow us on Twitter, Instagram and TikTok.

notes.title: VIP Characters 👑 Fable Hospital Dev Diary #3
notes.content:
Hello future manager of medieval hospitals,

In previous development diaries, we have shared who your future employees and patients will be. In today’s update, we introduce you to a special type of character: the VIP visitors!

From time to time, we will receive special visits for which we must be prepared. An ancient and powerful god will drop by our hospital to see how things are going. And it’s best to be prepared: they are profoundly demanding of their subjects (not so much of themselves).

We might receive visits from:


 Zeus ⚡
 Odin ❄️
 Ra ☀️
 Hades 🔥
 Quetzalcoatl  🦅
 Inari  🦊
 Wukong 🐒


The VIP characters add an extra layer of depth to managing your hospital. This gives you an additional incentive to always strive for optimal performance, presenting a constant challenge that rewards you generously when everything runs as it should (or almost does).

Interesting? Follow us on Twitter, Instagram and TikTok.

notes.title: Patients 💉 Fable Hospital Dev Diary #2
notes.content:
Hello future manager of medieval hospitals,

We have already introduced you to the unusual cast of doctors and workers that will be at your disposal. Today, we share with you those who always have the last word: the clients, the patients of Fable Hospital. Spoiler: get ready to treat terrifyingly... well, just terrifying diseases.

Fable Hospital is a management game where you take charge of a hospital in a medieval fantasy world. And aren’t patients what give meaning to every good hospital? Don’t forget to add Fable Hospital to your wishlist to stay updated with all the news.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Decapitated

The great advantage of this patient is that his "illness" is easy to diagnose. It’s obvious at first glance. The problem? Well, his head is not attached to the rest of his body. He requires rather bold remedies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/9a9aed9487ae54e32255240aec5b4e722b7d7b16.png

Zombie

The kind of patient that doctors love the most: never complains, and if they do, it’s completely unintelligible. They don’t need anesthesia, or at least it seems so. Almost all advantages, the big challenge is enduring the smell they emit.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/ddb852e9af67e5ec652769ab1b102543b144992c.png

Skeleton

Everyone thinks that in his previous life he was a pirate, but no one has been able to confirm it. No one knows either if his previous life had anything to do with his current illness: the complete lack of skin, organs, and muscles. He never parts from his hat.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/a05a7b27e418eb7cfe7c9281dbcffc23c929a3cb.png

Dark Fairy

She’s going through a phase, or at least that’s what her parents claim. As for her, she vehemently denies it. Butterfly wings, heart of a venomous spider. She flies but not much, never rises more than a few centimeters off the ground.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/16e6502a0da41ce1a6953f868687379910599135.png

Werewolf

He has a love-hate relationship with the moon. The most hated by the rest of the patients: he spends the night howling and doesn’t let anyone sleep. Feeding them is more expensive than any possible treatment they receive. And on more than one occasion, they confuse their doctor’s hand with a food dish.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/0ed73fc5312461c603b8b7b9e8c6393b94527c95.png

Minotaur

They are usually unbearable: they think of themselves as living legends, narcissistic to the extreme. To their credit, they have millennia-old anecdotes. They have a strange obsession with red fabrics.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/d4a4be1e77b0ec60be7bebfdd68603b9c80fa669.png

Mummy

The quintessential elderly patient. He is (literally) older than the pyramids. His joints creak as if they haven’t moved in 4000 years. And most likely, that’s the case. He’s the only patient who already comes bandaged from home.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/327509b395707a6af2f6942f9683d8c6c19285ce.png

Orc

He has the intellectual capacity of a rock. Adding two plus two is a challenge for him. The mind of a 2-year-old in the body of an Olympic weightlifting champion. Weapons are not allowed in the hospital, but no one has dared to enforce this rule with him.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/745f8f3eb06416140d839ddab4c3cfeaa3e40918.png

Possessed

Everyone knows there is something evil inside her body, but no one really knows what. Her gaze competes in coldness with her heart. Practically all doctors fear her (due to her bad temper). She never parts from her teddy bear (unfortunately, it smells awful).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/f3a47000c51361093b10087d6495ba9825d5c3ff.png

Vampire

The living (or almost) proof that vampires exist. He dresses and behaves like an aristocrat, but no one takes him seriously. He thinks he is much scarier than he actually is (not at all). He tries unsuccessfully to scare the hospital staff, usually making a fool of himself with his refined manners.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/85227fa8c40f0cc215c5164050e41642230c6f3a.png

Interesting? Follow us on Twitter, Instagram and TikTok.

notes.title: Doctors & Workers ⚕️ Fable Hospital Dev Diary #1
notes.content:
Hello, future manager of medieval hospitals,

What would a hospital be without a stellar cast of doctors with solid academic training, extensive experience, and impeccable ethics? Well, you're about to find out because the doctors at your disposal in Fable Hospital will be... Well, let's say... peculiar.

Fable Hospital is a management game where you take charge of a hospital in a medieval fantasy world. As a good director, the selection and management of staff will be crucial for the proper functioning of your facility. You might even end up curing some patients, who knows.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726060/Fable_Hospital/

Below, we share with you the different types of doctors and workers that you'll have at your disposal in Fable Hospital.

Doctors

Plague Doctor
The only one with knowledge slightly similar to medicine. He cures 50% of his patients and kills the other 50%, a surprisingly better average than his colleagues. He is convinced of the health benefits of bad odors. What a cheap excuse for poor hygiene.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/259c800db72823c789a104e07bfd88a2677a1b61.png

Druid
His favorite remedies are infusions and music. Unfortunately for his patients, his infusions taste like dirt, and his musical abilities are on par with those of a deaf cat. To a druid, magic and gardening are the same thing.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/9d2f11a9e0fc029e362fc6ebcfcaf404d39f7ad8.png

Alchemist
The world's foremost expert in succeeding by failing. The worse his formulas' results, the more likely they are to end up curing the patient. Side effects are... secondary. Who cares if your skin changes color, the number of fingers on one hand isn't usual, or you lose an ear. The important thing is getting cured.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/feb1545bcf4bd74fa81bad807a24e2043412f892.png

Fortune Teller
She is a master of future knowledge. But she can't differentiate between the important parts and the trivial details. Well, no one is perfect. By the way, her obsession with the evil eye as the cause of all known diseases doesn't help.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/cd13ef946f82b7c1c324f20e9c77f55877b4830c.png

Mad Engineer
He is convinced that he will change the world with his next invention. And he certainly will: to a smokier and more explosion-filled place. Skilled like few others in the art of creating things that almost work.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/0d97efb80aaf4a86df762fd4b806b160529824e4.png

Torturer
When you hear him talk about "alternative therapies," you know what he means. He is the best at making his patients talk, though always in an incomprehensible manner. "If it hurts, it means it's healing" as a way of life.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/021dd283ed9df393f8a2307af27639a396ac6e9c.png

Friar
Always willing to pray for your soul and your health. A staunch defender of moderation with a glass of wine in hand. He has a tendency to prescribe "a fun afternoon" as a cure for almost everything (this afternoon includes large amounts of wine).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/1f8b6e5ba40200020e497bc3c2559a4b89ff5937.png

Nuns
Ancient healing methods, recipes with centuries of "proven" effectiveness. They dedicate their lives to caring for others as long as your health improves quickly; their patience runs out quickly (especially if a Friar drinks their wine).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/c0502e5b6e5d2350cbf08081d81c99a334603816.png

Wizard
He is wise and reflective, always invoking the right magic, though his healing spells produce a slight burning smell in the patients. He dresses like a solemn wizard but his true specialty is card tricks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/a4a2ed4458a7d543ab43b0a3eaa745f7a11c0bbd.png

Workers

Gatherer Goblins
They work tirelessly and never talk about working conditions. By working, they mean collecting all kinds of things. And by all kinds of things, I mean EVERYTHING, even those with an owner. Their concept of ownership is, let's say... flexible.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/0ba997cb17f9abd9cc28aceff2ede28db8fe6c4d.png

Hunchback Janitor

Frighteningly efficient in keeping the hospital clean. His cleaning method inevitably involves scaring the patients. This doesn't make him very popular among them, but he is undoubtedly the favorite of rats and other rodents.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/5238adbaae112e5b26187dd4e5f4256dafdae452.png

Brewmaster
The most beloved employee in the hospital. He prescribes beer as a cure as lightly as he samples his own brews. His only weak point is his inability to measure the potency of his beer, which usually has more degrees than a stew in August.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/8143e48ad8d58a3492149a0bc08c1a8920092233.png

Baker
She is capable of turning flour, water, and yeast into a healing miracle. Sometimes she even adds sugar, though no one is sure if it's too much. Most of her bread is so hard that you could knock down a troll with a single blow, but that's a minor detail.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/98a7a9637d7eb2e578d25892efd36ccf6ec93797.png

Leprechaun
His storytelling skills reach unimaginable limits: some patients manage to get cured just by listening to him narrate, the rest simply fall asleep. The problem? His fondness for practical jokes. The poor patients who fall asleep often end up with their faces marked.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44784410/4e7d63c6c17e8d690e8496cce8efe333341510c3.png

Looking good? Keep an eye in our Twitter, Instagram and TikTok accounts for more!
